literal: Among things obtained, that which we know is not; other than the blessing of children who have known knowledge, other things.
translation: Among all the things one can acquire, we know of no greater blessing than having children who possess wisdom.
modern: ஒருவர் பெறும் செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றுள்ளும், அறிவுடைய பிள்ளைகளைப் பெறும் பேற்றினைத் தவிர வேறு சிறந்த பேறு இருப்பதாக நாம் அறியவில்லை.
explanation: This couplet evaluates the greatest possible acquisition in human life. The phrase 'பெறும் அவற்றுள்' (among things obtained) sets up a comparison of all forms of wealth, status, or possessions. The poet emphatically states 'யாம் அறிவது இல்லை' (we know of nothing) to dismiss all other achievements. The true treasure is defined as 'அறிவு அறிந்த மக்கட்பேறு' (the blessing of children who possess knowledge). Here, the repetition of the root for knowledge emphasizes not just having offspring, but raising children who have actively cultivated wisdom and good character.
